sections.content: How many people are "houseparents and residential wardens"?

32,970 people

were counted on the census as "houseparents and residential wardens" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Houseparents and residential wardens are responsible for the care and supervision of children and the elderly within residential homes, schools or their own homes.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "houseparents and residential wardens" there were more women than men (80.8% compared with 19.2%).

This means "houseparents and residential wardens" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "caring personal service occupations".

Men made up 19.2% and women made up 80.8% of "houseparents and residential wardens"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "houseparents and residential wardens" included:

  • office managers
  • care escorts
  • animal care services occupations (other)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "houseparents and residential wardens" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "houseparents and residential wardens", 21.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "houseparents and residential wardens" was 16 to 19 years.

  • driving instructors

We can look at who worked as "houseparents and residential wardens" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "houseparents and residential wardens" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "houseparents and residential wardens", 14.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (90.1% compared with 9.9%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (73.2%) than an employee (26.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
